behaviours.title: Deposit credits the exact amount, cents kept
behaviours.when: 100.5 is deposited to account A with txnId d1
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) is 100.5
behaviours.contrary_then: balance(A) is 100 (the cents are dropped)
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected and balance(A) stays 0
balance(A) is 101 (rounded to whole units)

behaviours.title: Amounts are rounded half-up to the nearest cent
behaviours.when: 10.005 is deposited to A
behaviours.then: balance(A) is 10.01
behaviours.contrary_then: balance(A) is 10 (the half cent is dropped)
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected because it has more than two decimals
balance(A) is 10.005 (no rounding)

behaviours.title: A deposit that rounds to zero cents is accepted and recorded as 0
behaviours.when: 0.004 is deposited to A with txnId d1
behaviours.then: the result is ok, balance(A) is 0 and entries(A) holds one deposit entry with amount 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected with reason amount-too-small
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted but no entry is recorded
the deposit is rounded up and balance(A) becomes 0.01

behaviours.title: A deposit of 0 is rejected
behaviours.when: 0 is deposited to A
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance(A) stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted (ok) as a no-op
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with a different reason such as amount-too-small

behaviours.title: A negative deposit is rejected
behaviours.when: -50 is deposited to A
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance(A) stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit goes through and balance(A) becomes -50
contrary_alternatives: the sign is ignored and balance(A) becomes 50

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit txnId is ignored but reported ok
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 100 was deposited to A with txnId d1
behaviours.when: 100 is deposited to A with txnId d1 again
behaviours.then: the result is ok, balance(A) stays 100 and A has only one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is applied again and balance(A) becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a duplicate reason and balance(A) stays 100

behaviours.title: Amount validation happens before duplicate detection
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 100 was deposited to A with txnId d1
behaviours.when: -5 is deposited to A with txnId d1
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the call is reported ok because d1 was already seen
contrary_alternatives: the call is rejected with a duplicate-transaction reason

behaviours.title: A txnId used by a deposit makes a later withdrawal with the same txnId a no-op
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 100 was deposited to A with txnId x
behaviours.when: 10 is withdrawn from A with txnId x
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through and balance(A) becomes 89.5
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected as a duplicate transaction and balance(A) stays 100

behaviours.title: Opening an existing account does not reset it
behaviours.given: a Ledger where A was opened and 100 deposited
behaviours.when: open(A) is called again
behaviours.then: balance(A) stays 100 and its single entry is kept
behaviours.contrary_then: balance(A) resets to 0 and its entries are cleared
contrary_alternatives: opening an existing account throws an error

behaviours.title: An unknown account reads as balance 0 with no entries
behaviours.when: balance(Z) and entries(Z) are read for never-used account Z
behaviours.then: balance is 0 and entries is an empty list
behaviours.contrary_then: reading an unknown account throws an error
contrary_alternatives: balance returns undefined for unknown accounts

behaviours.title: Small withdrawals pay the minimum fee of 0.50
behaviours.when: 10 is withdrawn from A with txnId w1
behaviours.then: the result is ok, balance(A) is 89.5 and the withdrawal entry amount is 10.5 (amount plus fee)
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is 1% (0.10) and balance(A) becomes 89.9
contrary_alternatives: no fee is charged and balance(A) becomes 90
the withdrawal is refused as below a minimum amount

behaviours.title: Withdrawal fee is 1% of the amount
behaviours.when: 100 is withdrawn from A
behaviours.then: the fee is 1.00 and balance(A) is 99
behaviours.contrary_then: only the minimum fee 0.50 applies and balance(A) becomes 99.5
contrary_alternatives: the fee is 2% and balance(A) becomes 98
no fee is charged and balance(A) becomes 100

behaviours.title: Withdrawal fee is rounded up to the next cent
behaviours.when: 100.01 is withdrawn from A
behaviours.then: the fee is 1.01 and balance(A) is 98.98
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is rounded down to 1.00 and balance(A) becomes 98.99
contrary_alternatives: the fee is rounded to the nearest cent (1.00) and balance(A) becomes 98.99

behaviours.title: Withdrawal fee is capped at 25
behaviours.when: 3000 is withdrawn from A
behaviours.then: the fee is 25 and balance(A) is 1975
behaviours.contrary_then: the uncapped 1% fee of 30 applies and balance(A) becomes 1970
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected for exceeding a single-withdrawal limit and balance(A) stays 5000

behaviours.title: A withdrawal that uses the whole balance including fee is allowed
behaviours.when: 100 is withdrawn from A (100 plus fee 1 = 101)
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'insufficient-funds'
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal goes through but must leave a minimum balance, so it is refused

behaviours.title: A withdrawal whose amount plus fee exceeds the balance by one cent is rejected
behaviours.when: 100 is withdrawn from A (needs 101 with fee)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance(A) stays 100.99
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through and balance(A) becomes -0.01
contrary_alternatives: the funds check ignores the fee, so the withdrawal goes through and balance(A) becomes -0.01
the fee is reduced to what is left and balance(A) becomes 0

behaviours.title: Withdrawals are limited to 5000 in total; the next cent is refused
behaviours.given: A has balance 10000 and has already withdrawn 5000 with txnId w1 (balance now 4975)
behaviours.when: 0.01 is withdrawn from A with txnId w2
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance(A) stays 4975
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through (ok) and balance(A) becomes 4974.49
contrary_alternatives: the limit is 10000 so the withdrawal goes through

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal above 5000 is refused
behaviours.when: 5000.01 is withdrawn from A
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance(A) stays 10000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through (ok) and balance(A) becomes 4974.99
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is capped at 5000 and processed

behaviours.title: Fees do not count toward the 5000 withdrawal limit, and reaching exactly 5000 is allowed
behaviours.given: A has balance 10000 and withdrew 4990 (fee 25) with txnId w1
behaviours.when: 10 is withdrawn from A with txnId w2, bringing the total withdrawn to exactly 5000
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) is 4974.5
behaviours.contrary_then: fees count toward the limit, so the withdrawal is refused with 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: the limit is exclusive, so reaching exactly 5000 is refused with 'daily-limit'

behaviours.title: Insufficient funds is reported before the withdrawal limit
behaviours.given: A has balance 6000 and withdrew 5000 with txnId w1 (balance now 975)
behaviours.when: 2000 is withdrawn from A with txnId w2 (over both the balance and the limit)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance(A) stays 975
behaviours.contrary_then: the result reason is 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance goes negative

behaviours.title: A rejected withdrawal does not use up its txnId
behaviours.given: A has balance 5; withdrawing 10 with txnId w1 was rejected; then 100 more was deposited
behaviours.when: 10 is withdrawn from A with txnId w1 again
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) is 94.5
behaviours.contrary_then: the retry is treated as an already-seen transaction: ok but balance(A) stays 105
contrary_alternatives: the retry is rejected as a duplicate transaction and balance(A) stays 105

behaviours.title: A withdrawal of 0 is rejected
behaviours.when: 0 is withdrawn from A
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance(A) stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted (ok) and the minimum fee is charged, leaving 99.5
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted as a no-op and balance(A) stays 100

behaviours.title: Repeating a withdrawal txnId is ignored
behaviours.given: A has balance 100 and withdrew 10 with txnId w1 (balance 89.5)
behaviours.when: 10 is withdrawn from A with txnId w1 again
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) stays 89.5
behaviours.contrary_then: the second withdrawal is also applied and balance(A) becomes 79
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected as a duplicate and balance(A) stays 89.5

behaviours.title: Transferring the whole balance succeeds with no fee
behaviours.given: A has balance 100 and B is new
behaviours.when: 100 is transferred from A to B with txnId t1
behaviours.then: the result is ok; A is 0, B is 100; A has a transfer-out entry of 100 and B a transfer-in entry of 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected with 'insufficient-funds' because a fee would be due
contrary_alternatives: the transfer goes through but a fee is taken so B receives 99

behaviours.title: A transfer one cent above the balance is rejected
behaviours.when: 100.01 is transferred from A to B
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }; A stays 100 and B stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer goes through (ok) and A becomes -0.01
contrary_alternatives: a partial transfer of 100 is made

behaviours.title: A transfer of 0 is rejected
behaviours.when: 0 is transferred from A to B
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is accepted (ok) as a no-op
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is rejected with 'insufficient-funds'

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer txnId is ignored
behaviours.given: A has balance 100 and 30 was transferred to B with txnId t1
behaviours.when: 30 is transferred from A to B with txnId t1 again
behaviours.then: the result is ok; A stays 70 and B stays 30
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied twice: A becomes 40 and B 60
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected as a duplicate and balances stay 70 and 30

behaviours.title: Split gives leftover cents to the first recipients in list order
behaviours.when: 1.00 is split from A to [B, C, D] with txnId s1
behaviours.then: the result is ok; A is 0; B gets 0.34, C 0.33, D 0.33
behaviours.contrary_then: the leftover cent goes to the last recipient: B 0.33, C 0.33, D 0.34
contrary_alternatives: the leftover cent stays with A (A 0.01, each recipient 0.33)
the split is rejected because it does not divide evenly

behaviours.title: A split smaller than the number of recipients leaves the last recipient with 0
behaviours.when: 0.02 is split from A to [B, C, D] with txnId s1
behaviours.then: the result is ok; A is 0.98; B gets 0.01, C gets 0.01, D gets 0 but still has a split-in entry of 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is rejected as too small to divide
contrary_alternatives: each recipient gets 0 and A keeps the 0.02
D gets no entry at all

behaviours.title: A split with no recipients is rejected
behaviours.when: 10 is split from A to []
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'no-recipients' } and A stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is accepted (ok) as a no-op
contrary_alternatives: the amount is debited from A and goes nowhere

behaviours.title: Split amount is validated before recipients
behaviours.when: 0 is split from A to []
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result reason is 'no-recipients'
contrary_alternatives: the split is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: A split above the balance is rejected
behaviours.when: 100.01 is split from A to [B, C]
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }; A stays 100 and B stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the split goes through (ok) and A becomes -0.01
contrary_alternatives: only the available 100 is split

behaviours.title: Splitting the whole balance is allowed
behaviours.when: 100 is split from A to [B, C]
behaviours.then: the result is ok; A is 0, B is 50 and C is 50
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is rejected with 'insufficient-funds'
contrary_alternatives: a fee is taken and each recipient gets less than 50

behaviours.title: Repeating a split txnId is ignored
behaviours.given: A has balance 100 and split 10 to [B, C] with txnId s1
behaviours.when: 10 is split to [B, C] with txnId s1 again
behaviours.then: the result is ok; A stays 90, B 5 and C 5
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is applied twice: A becomes 80, B 10, C 10
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected as a duplicate and balances are unchanged

behaviours.title: Interest for 365 days at 5% on 1000 is exactly 50
behaviours.when: applyInterest(A, 5, 365, i1) is called
behaviours.then: the result is ok, balance(A) is 1050 and an interest entry of 50 is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: a 360-day year is used and balance(A) becomes 1050.69
contrary_alternatives: interest is compounded daily giving about 1051.27
interest is refused because the balance was not held for a full year

behaviours.title: Interest is rounded down to the cent
behaviours.when: applyInterest(A, 5, 30, i1) is called (exact interest 4.10958…)
behaviours.then: balance(A) is 1004.1
behaviours.contrary_then: interest is rounded to nearest (up) giving 1004.11
contrary_alternatives: a 360-day year is used giving 1004.16

behaviours.title: Interest under one cent is a silent no-op and does not use up the txnId
behaviours.when: applyInterest(A, 1, 1, i1) is called, then 5 is deposited to A with txnId i1
behaviours.then: the interest call is ok with no entry added, and the later deposit with i1 is applied: balance(A) is 6
behaviours.contrary_then: the interest call consumes i1, so the later deposit is ignored and balance(A) stays 1
contrary_alternatives: the interest call is rejected with 'amount-too-small'
a minimum of 0.01 interest is credited

behaviours.title: An interest rate of 0 is rejected
behaviours.when: applyInterest(A, 0, 30, i1) is called
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the call is accepted (ok) as a no-op
contrary_alternatives: the call is rejected with a different reason such as invalid-rate

behaviours.title: Interest over 0 days is rejected
behaviours.when: applyInterest(A, 5, 0, i1) is called
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the call is accepted (ok) as a no-op
contrary_alternatives: one day of interest is applied

behaviours.title: Repeating an interest txnId is ignored
behaviours.given: A has balance 1000 and 5% for 365 days was applied with txnId i1 (balance 1050)
behaviours.when: applyInterest(A, 5, 365, i1) is called again
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) stays 1050
behaviours.contrary_then: interest is applied again and balance(A) becomes 1102.5
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected as a duplicate

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit credits amount times rate as a deposit
behaviours.when: depositForeign(A, 100, 1.1, f1) is called
behaviours.then: the result is ok, balance(A) is 110 and the entry is kind 'deposit' with amount 110
behaviours.contrary_then: the rate is applied as a division and balance(A) becomes 90.91
contrary_alternatives: the raw 100 is credited, ignoring the rate
the deposit is rejected

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit with rate 0 is rejected
behaviours.when: depositForeign(A, 100, 0, f1) is called
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result reason is 'amount-too-small'
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted with 0 credited

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit of amount 0 is rejected
behaviours.when: depositForeign(A, 0, 1.5, f1) is called
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted (ok) as a no-op
contrary_alternatives: the result reason is 'amount-too-small'

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit that converts to under half a cent is rejected and records nothing
behaviours.when: depositForeign(A, 0.001, 1, f1) is called
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'amount-too-small' } and entries(A) is empty
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted (ok) with 0 credited
contrary_alternatives: the amount is rounded up to 0.01 and credited

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit converting to exactly half a cent rounds up to 0.01
behaviours.when: depositForeign(A, 10, 0.0005, f1) is called (converted value 0.005)
behaviours.then: the result is ok and balance(A) is 0.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the half cent is dropped and the deposit is rejected with 'amount-too-small'
contrary_alternatives: it is accepted but credited as 0

behaviours.title: Repeating a foreign deposit txnId is ignored, even if the repeat would be too small
behaviours.given: A received depositForeign of 100 at rate 2 with txnId f1 (balance 200)
behaviours.when: depositForeign(A, 100, 2, f1) and then depositForeign(A, 0.001, 1, f1) are called
behaviours.then: both calls return ok and balance(A) stays 200
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is applied and balance(A) becomes 400
contrary_alternatives: the tiny repeat is rejected with 'amount-too-small'
the repeat is rejected as a duplicate
